macro_regime: Late-cycle with an exogenous energy supply shock: US-Iran/Strait of Hormuz conflict has crude elevated (CL $78.18, +8.5% 1m; BZ $83.55, +9.5% 1m, as of 2026-08-07 close), US inflation re-accelerating (C-CPI-U +3.4% y/y per BLS July release), Fed on hold with hike risk (Warsh Fed; iShares/JPM research note market now pricing possible hikes vs cuts expected at year-start), BoC held at 2.25% on 2026-07-15 with an explicit hiking bias on energy inflation.
thesis_summary: Long Canada vs. the world as the cleanest listed expression of the Hormuz oil shock. Canada is the G10's energy exporter: crude +8.5% in a month is a direct terms-of-trade windfall, the BoC's 2.25% floor with a hike bias supports CAD, and EWC's energy/materials/banks stack is exactly the value-commodity complex this regime rewards — while the EWC/ACWI ratio sits at only the 62nd percentile of its 52-week range, well below the crowded IWD/IWF expression of the same regime at the 94th.
thesis_detail: The macro regime has shifted from the cuts-expected soft landing priced at the start of 2026 to an inflation-scare hold with two-sided hike risk, driven by the Middle East energy shock. That regime punishes duration/growth (IWD/IWF +9.6% over 3m confirms the market already believes this) and rewards commodity-linked value. The cleanest remaining entry is geographic, not factoral: the value/growth ratio is already at the 94th percentile of its 52-week range — chasing it here is buying the extension, not the regime. EWC/ACWI at 0.3797 (62nd percentile, +2.1% 1m) offers the same commodity-value exposure with room to the 52-week high of 0.3993. Fundamentals: BoC at 2.25% (held 2026-07-15, per bankofcanada.ca) with the market assigning non-trivial hike odds to the September meeting as energy inflation feeds through, while the Fed's hold-with-hike-risk stance caps US multiple expansion. Canadian housing is stabilizing (May 2026 GDP positive on housing industry growth; ~20% uptick in purchases since spring per True North), removing the key domestic drag on the banks-heavy index. Hedge structure: short ACWI strips global equity beta, leaving the Canada-vs-world terms-of-trade and rate-differential differential — ACWI is ~65% US, so the hedge is short the most rate-sensitive, energy-importing major market against the energy exporter. Flip condition: a durable Hormuz de-escalation/ceasefire that takes Brent back below $72, or a global growth scare that hits commodities broadly — either breaks the terms-of-trade leg.

base_case: Conflict stays simmering without resolution; crude holds $75-85; BoC holds with hawkish talk into September while the Fed stays on hold; EWC grinds toward the top of its 52-week ratio range as earnings from Canadian energy and banks benefit from the commodity bid. Ratio to ~0.395 (+4%).
bull_case: Hormuz escalation or sustained supply disruption takes Brent above $95; BoC signals or delivers a hike in September; CAD rallies; ratio breaks the 52-week high toward 0.41 (+8%).
bear_case: Ceasefire/de-escalation collapses the crude risk premium (Brent back to high $60s) and the energy trade unwinds; or a global growth scare hits all commodities. Ratio retraces through 0.3700 toward the 0.3550 range floor — thesis invalid, stop takes us out.
key_risks: Headline-driven: a single ceasefire announcement can gap the ratio through the stop overnight; crude risk premium is the thesis
Canadian mortgage-renewal wall re-asserts if BoC actually hikes, hitting the 35%-weight banks complex
Global growth scare (US hard landing on re-tightened financial conditions) hits commodities and EWC beta together, overwhelming the terms-of-trade leg
US trade policy escalation toward Canada remains a live tail (cited by BoC in July statement)
